formal_statement: ∃ (x1 : ℕ), ∀ (x2 : ℕ) (x3 : SimpleGraph (Fin x2)) [x4 : DecidableRel x3.Adj] (x5 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ (x6 : Fin x2) (x7 : x3.Walk x6 x6), x7.IsCycle → (5 : ℕ) ≤ x7.length) → PEqualNP.TopForm.IsLeastAO x3 x5 → PEqualNP.TopForm.TopForm x3 x5 → {x9 ∈ PEqualNP.TopForm.Ustar x3 x5 | ∃ (x10 : Fin x2) (x11 : Fin x2), x9 = s(x10, x11) ∧ ∃ x12 ∈ PEqualNP.TopForm.tops x3 x5, ∃ (x13 : Fin (2 : ℕ)), ∃ x14 ∈ PEqualNP.TopForm.junk x3 x5, x10 ∈ PEqualNP.TopForm.side x5 x12 x13 ∧ PEqualNP.CleanedNonEdge.OrReaches x2 x5 (PEqualNP.TopForm.opnd x5 x12 ((1 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) - x13)) x14 ∧ PEqualNP.EdgeOwnership.gateVal x2 x5 x14 (PEqualNP.EdgeOwnership.pairInput x10 x11) = Bool.true}.card ≤ x1 * (x5.size + (1 : ℕ))
plain_statement: A graph with no cycle shorter than 5; C a least circuit of AND and OR gates with exactly two inputs a gate for its edge function, in top form. The edges uv that are no top's cross pair and have a top with an end on one side and a junk AND true at input uv OR-reached from its other operand number at most c(gates+1), one c for all.
title: A step toward: Conjecture: circuits of AND and OR gates for the edge function of a graph with no cycle shorter than 5 have size linear in the number of edges
